newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks seen opening firmer, await CPI.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks seen opening firmer, await CPI.

text.p: Jittery U.S. stocks were seen opening higher Thursday, but the market was waiting for this week's second batch of key inflation data, the consumer price index, to glean clues as to where they could be headed.
The consumer price index for July is due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, and is forecast to rise by 0.2 percent compared with June's 0.1 percent hike.
Although S&P 500 futures were firmer and pointed to a higher opening on Wall Street if the CPI came in as expected, current volatility in stocks made forecasting difficult.
The S&P 500 futures were up 2.30 at 928.10.
"The inflation numbers are not the problem. The problem is the more vigorous economy and the concern therein about the Federal Reserve," Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities said.
The Federal Reserve's open market committee meets next week to discuss interest rates.
Stocks have been spooked by indications that the U.S. economy is stronger than previously thought, raising fears of rate hikes.
The Dow closed 33 points lower at 7928 Wednesday.
The Dow was still struggling to absorb the heady gains of the past two months and this was contributing to the volatility, analysts said.
But despite the huge volatility Wednesday, the Dow lay at the beck and call of swings in bonds and currencies in the absence of any major corporate news.
"The Dow is the wildest I have seen it, but we had an even keel in advances and declines. The breadth is in an ordinary August trend," Wachtel said.
Stocks to watch Thursday included Micron Technology Inc, Wednesday's most heavily traded issue.
Micron was heavily sold after being downgraded by Merrill Lynch, but began to rebound overnight in London.
"We also need to watch if these beaten-down drug stocks show some bounce," an analyst said.
The dollar nudged higher against the yen on shortcovering in Tokyo, but trading was confined to a narrow range. The dollar was trading at 116.15/20.
In Europe, the dollar was holding above 1.83 marks in choppy, thin trade as the currency markets awaited the U.S. consumer price index Thursday. The dollar was trading at 1.8350/57 marks.
Japan's Nikkei 225 index closed up 214.02, or 1.13 percent, at 19,222.62. In London, the FTSE 100 was up 2.6 at 5006.2.
U.S. stocks in London were mostly firmer in light trading.

The Wall Street Journal said in its "Heard on the Street" column that only earlier this month Merrill Lynch's influential semi-conductor analyst Thomas Kurlak had told clients that semiconductor stocks looked good. On Wednesday he slashed his 1998 estimates for Micron Technology in half and the share price tumbled. Rumors are flying that Micron will be the first in a series of downgrades by Kurlak in coming weeks.
